items.q: A 34-year-old man crashes his motorcycle with pelvic fractures and a 2 cm arterial blush on CT. His pressure holds with fluids and his haemoglobin sags slowly. Which triage logic best sends this stable pelvic blush with sagging haemoglobin to radiology?
o: Stable blushes coil while unstable cases go to theatre
All pelvic fractures need immediate laparotomy
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Stable blushes coil while unstable cases go to theatre.** Stability buys mapping time where coils close blushes, while collapse demands surgical packing.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Stable cases gain from coiling
- C: Laparotomy misses arterial blushes
- D: Blushes bleed on without coils
**Key point:** Stable pelvic blushes embolise.
items.kp: Stable pelvic blushes go to embolisation.

items.q: A 29-year-old woman falls from a horse with a grade III splenic laceration and diffuse oozing. She stays stable with blood on board. The team coils her proximal splenic trunk. Which pressure-drop logic best explains proximal coiling for diffuse splenic oozing?
o: Lowered pressure lets torn branches clot while collaterals feed spleens
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Lowered pressure lets torn branches clot while collaterals feed spleens.** Trunk coils slow inflow so tears seal while short gastric branches keep spleens alive.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Coils preserve rather than remove
- C: Diffuse tears heal with pressure drops
- D: Stable bleeders still need control
**Key point:** Diffuse splenic oozing takes proximal coils.
items.kp: Diffuse splenic oozing suits proximal trunk coiling.

items.q: A 41-year-old man has a focal splenic pseudoaneurysm with an intact main trunk after a cricket ball injury. His spleen otherwise looks healthy. Which focal-sac logic best suits distal coils with trunk preservation here?
o: Pack the sac alone where trunks stay healthy
Coil the whole splenic trunk always
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Pack the sac alone where trunks stay healthy.** Focal sacs fill directly while intact trunks carry on feeding spleens normally.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Trunks need no sacrifice when healthy
- C: Healthy spleens stay put
- D: Large sacs rupture while watched
**Key point:** Focal sacs pack distally with trunks intact.
items.kp: Focal splenic sacs take distal packing with intact trunks.

items.q: A 38-year-old woman keeps her spleen after successful embolisation and asks about vaccines. The team explains that coiled spleens still immunise. Which immune-preservation logic best exempts embolised spleens from post-splenectomy vaccines?
o: Coiled spleens keep filtering immune tissue alive
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Coiled spleens keep filtering immune tissue alive.** Collateral-fed spleens continue clearing encapsulated germs, unlike removed organs that leave patients defenceless.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Vaccines stay safe regardless
- C: Immunity guards encapsulated germs
- D: Removed spleens need vaccines
**Key point:** Embolised spleens keep immune function.
items.kp: Embolised spleens keep immune function without vaccines.

items.q: A 45-year-old man has a grade IV liver laceration with a hepatic pseudoaneurysm on day-five surveillance. His portal flow looks reduced. The team packs the sac preserving the parent artery. Which dual-supply logic best demands parent preservation in injured livers?
o: Portal failure leaves arteries as the only lifeline
Sacrifice whole lobes for small sacs
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Portal failure leaves arteries as the only lifeline.** Injured livers with poor portal flow starve without arterial blood, so sacs fill while parents stay open.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Bile never feeds livers
- C: Parents carry whole lobes
- D: Lobes outlive small sacs
**Key point:** Injured livers keep parent arteries.
items.kp: Hepatic sacs pack with parents preserved.

items.q: A 52-year-old woman has a bleeding lower-pole renal laceration with a segmental blush after a fall. Her upper pole looks pristine with good function. Which nephron-sparing logic best suits segmental coils for bleeding renal poles?
o: Sacrifice bleeding poles while filtering tissue survives
Remove whole kidneys for pole bleeds
items.exp:

- C: Bleeds need closing

items.kp: Bleeding renal poles take segmental coils with sparing.

items.q: A 31-year-old man has an unstable pelvic fracture with pressure collapsing despite blood, and no CT possible. The surgeons pack the pelvis in theatre. Which instability logic best sends collapsing pelvises to surgical packing over coils?
o: Unstable cases need theatre packing without mapping delays
Unstable patients wait for CT always
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Unstable cases need theatre packing without mapping delays.** Collapsing patients die during scanner trips while packing tamponades venous bone bleeding directly.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Collapse forbids scanner trips
- C: Packing tamponades bone bleeding
- D: CT waits kill collapsers
**Key point:** Unstable pelvises pack surgically.
items.kp: Unstable pelvic fractures go to surgical packing.

items.q: A 36-year-old woman stabilises then sags repeatedly with transient responses to blood. Both surgeons and radiologists stand ready. Which hybrid logic best serves this transient responder with repeated sagging?
o: Map with surgeons scrubbed nearby for instant conversion
Treat transient response as full recovery
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Map with surgeons scrubbed nearby for instant conversion.** Transient responders flip to collapse without warning, so coils proceed with theatres ready.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Home discharges kill saggers
- C: Teams stay till bleeding ends
- D: Transience warns of collapse
**Key point:** Transient responders need hybrid readiness.
items.kp: Transient responders need hybrid surgeon-radiology readiness.

items.q: A 43-year-old man develops a large urinoma compressing his ureter after renal embolisation for trauma. His creatinine climbs with obstruction. Which collection logic best drains compressing urinomas after renal injury?
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Percutaneous drainage releasing obstructing collections.** Urine collections strangle ureters where tube drainage relieves pressure without organ loss.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Obstruction injures kidneys progressively
- C: Coils never drain fluid
- D: Collections rarely need removal
**Key point:** Obstructing urinomas drain percutaneously.
items.kp: Compressing urinomas need percutaneous drainage.

items.q: A 47-year-old woman has her high-grade splenic injury re-scanned before discharge with sealed vessels and a viable spleen. She asks about activity. Which healing-protection logic best restricts activity for weeks after splenic salvage?
o: Healing capsules rupture again under strain within weeks
Bed rest cures all injuries alone
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Healing capsules rupture again under strain within weeks.** Clot-filled tears need weeks to scar firmly, and early strain bursts them into delayed catastrophe.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Healing takes weeks not instants
- C: Strain bursts fresh clots
- D: Rest protects rather than cures
**Key point:** Healed spleens need weeks of protection.
items.kp: Splenic salvage needs weeks of activity restriction.

items.q: A 50-year-old man has an open pelvic fracture with contamination after a crush injury and a stable arterial blush. Coils stop the bleeding. Which contamination logic best pairs antibiotics with embolisation in open pelvic fractures?

items.exp:
**Answer: A - Cover brewing infection while coils stop arterial bleeding.** Contaminated fractures seed bacteria where drugs guard tissue while coils shut vessels.

- C: Open fractures infect readily
- D: Coils carry no antibiotics
**Key point:** Open fractures pair coils with antibiotics.
items.kp: Open pelvic fractures need coils with antibiotics.

items.q: A 33-year-old woman at 30 weeks gestation falls with a splenic blush but stable vitals. Shielding and low-dose mapping guide her coiling. Which pregnancy-trauma logic best balances mother and fetus in stable splenic bleeding?

Withhold all maternal treatment for fetal sake
Maximum dose imaging for clearest pictures
items.exp:

**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Withholding kills mothers and fetuses
- C: Maximum dose harms fetuses vainly
- D: Delivery suits obstetric reasons
**Key point:** Pregnant trauma treats mothers shielded.
items.kp: Pregnant stable trauma embolises with shielding.

items.q: A 58-year-old man has bilateral internal iliac blushes after a crush injury. The operator coils both sides sequentially. Which bilateral logic best justifies closing both internal iliac trunks in bleeding pelvises?

items.q: A 39-year-old man re-bleeds from his spleen on day three with falling haemoglobin after initial coiling. Repeat CT shows a new blush beside old coils. Which failure logic best re-maps post-coil splenic re-bleeds?

items.q: A 62-year-old man has a shattered splenic hilum with no salvageable tissue on CT and ongoing collapse. Surgeons remove the spleen promptly. Which unsalvageable logic best sends shattered hila to surgery over coils?
o: Destroyed hila hold no coils and bleed on

items.q: A 35-year-old woman has a renal pseudoaneurysm with haematuria two weeks after a fall. Her kidney function stays normal. Which delayed-sac logic best explains late haematuria from post-traumatic renal pseudoaneurysms?
o: Walled sacs rupture late into collecting systems

- D: Late bleeds still need coils

items.kp: Delayed haematuria after trauma means ruptured renal pseudoaneurysm.

- D: Buttocks ache transiently

- C: Portal tears bleed massively
- D: Arteries need shutting
